fact: The course covers the relationship between hardware and software, the organization of the CPU, memory hierarchy, input/output mechanisms, instruction execution, and performance measurement
Students will learn how computers are designed, how they execute programs, and how architectural choices affect system performance
The first recommended textbook is Computer Organization and Architecture, 11th Edition, by William Stallings, Pearson Education, 2019, one of the most widely used undergraduate textbooks

Other recommended textbooks are Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface by David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy, Structured Computer Organization by Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Essentials of Computer Organization and Architecture by Linda Null and Julia Lobur, and Computer Organization, Design, and Architecture by Sajjan G. Shiva

Computers have had a huge impact on the manner in which society operates, and increased efficiency through automation and organization only scratches the surface of what computing technology has afforded humanity
The technology has progressed so much that people not utilizing computing technology in their businesses are at a disadvantage
Definition 1: a computer is a programmable device that stores, retrieves, and processes data
Definition 2: a computer is a machine or device that performs processes, calculations and operations based on instructions provided by a software or hardware program

Definition 3: a computer may be defined as a sophisticated electronic calculating machine that accepts data, processes the data according to a list of internally stored instructions and produces the resulting output information
For the most part all personal computers consist of the same basic components: Central Processing Unit (CPU), memory, circuit board, storage, and input/output devices
Almost every digital device uses the same set of components, so examining the personal computer gives insight into the structure of a variety of digital devices
Thinking about computers in terms of their basic components, and the functionality associated with each component, reveals the primary functions of the computer in general
Computer systems are designed using two closely related but distinct concepts, computer architecture and computer organization, which define how a computer system functions and operates internally
Computer architecture refers simply to the attributes of a computer visible to a programmer, that is, those attributes that have a direct impact on the logical execution of a computer program

It is an architectural design issue whether a computer will have a multiply instruction, but an organizational issue whether that instruction is implemented by a special multiply unit or by a mechanism that makes repeated use of the add unit
Computer architecture refers to the functional design and logical structure of a computer system, and describes the instruction set, data types, addressing modes and register organization
Computer architecture answers the question: what does the computer do, and it therefore serves as a blueprint for system design

Examples of architectural attributes include the instruction set, the number of bits used to represent various data types such as numbers and characters, I/O mechanisms, and techniques for addressing memory
The lecture poses the in-class question: what is the primary focus of computer architecture?
Computer architecture focuses on the functional behavior and logical design of the computer system
Computer organization refers to the operational units and their interconnections that realize the architectural specifications
Organizational attributes include those hardware details transparent to the programmer, such as control signals, interfaces between the computer and peripherals, and the memory technology used
Computer organization refers to the physical implementation of the system, including hardware components, interconnections, control signals and memory structure
Computer organization answers the question: how does the computer do it, and it ensures the architecture is translated into working hardware
Computer architecture can be likened to a building design while computer organization may be likened to the actual construction or implementation of the building
The lecture poses the in-class question: what does computer organization describe?
Computer organization describes the physical arrangement and implementation of hardware components

A computer system is not just a collection of hardware parts, it is a carefully designed system governed by computer architecture and computer organization, which together define what a computer system does and how efficiently it performs a task
Understanding the components of architecture and organization is crucial for designing efficient hardware systems, writing optimized software and improving system performance

Computer architecture defines the logical structure and functional behavior of a computer system, and its components are typically visible to programmers and determine how software interacts with hardware
In the smartphone example architecture defines the instruction set and data types, while organization determines speed, battery life and multitasking capability
Laptops may share the same architecture, such as x86, but have different organizations in cache size, RAM speed and CPU cores, with the result that they reach different performance levels
Architecture provides the blueprint and capabilities while organization determines efficiency and performance, and the two are deeply interconnected
Understanding both architecture and organization allows engineers to design better systems, programmers to write optimized code, and organizations to build high-performance computing solutions

In the revision summary, computer architecture describes the instruction set, data types, addressing modes and register organization and answers what does the computer do, while computer organization describes the operational units and their interconnections and answers how does the computer do it

The components of computer architecture are the Instruction Set Architecture, data types and representation, instruction set and format, addressing modes, register set, and system design, that is Von Neumann and Harvard architectures
The components of computer organization are the control unit, the ALU unit, memory organization, input/output systems, system buses and interconnections, and pipelining and parallelism
